messages:
marie: quick flag — longcontext benchmark shows steady memory growth attributed to KV cache fragmentation. repro: bench-longcontext --tokens=50000 on staging-r3.
marie: flame/heap snapshot attached in the run artifact, but high-level: free pool has many tiny holes and avg allocation ~320-420 bytes which rounds into 512-byte buckets today.
dan: ok can you paste the alloc summary? curious how bad the waste is.
marie: paste from the tracer dump:
```
KV alloc summary:
  total_cache_bytes: 3.2GB
  used_bytes: 2.6GB
  free_frag_bytes: 480MB
  small_chunks: 1.12M
  avg_chunk_size: 384
  bucket_counts: {256:128k, 512:740k, 1024:220k}
```
ashok: that matches an allocator inefficiency — many allocations sit just over 256 so they get bumped to 512. fragmentation + long-lived pinning from longcontexts -> leak-like growth.
sophia: do we know which codepaths are allocating at ~384? generation KV entries, right? token-level attention caches and some metadata.
marie: yes mostly attention KV + tokenizer metadata per layer. When batch sizes grow (we tested 16->64) reuse patterns change; larger batches increase short-lived overlap so reuse improves a bit, but long-tail single-session longcontext still churns microchunks.
dan: two angles: change allocator binning to include a 384/416 slab size or use subpage packing of small chunks. Or compaction: periodic coalescing pass to copy live entries into compacted slab.
ashok: subpage packing risks higher CPU during alloc/free; compaction risks copy overhead and stall impact. we can do background throttled compaction.
sophia: do we have perf counters for compaction cost vs memory saved? need a sim.
marie: I ran a quick sim copying 30% of free holes into consolidated slab during low qps; mem dropped ~320MB over 10m, CPU +5% per GPU host during background scan.
dan: +5% might be acceptable if bounded. Suggest heuristic: start compaction when free_frag > 200MB AND longcontext sessions > 1% of traffic. throttle with token budget per second.
ashok: also consider adaptive bin sizes: add intermediate bin at 384 and 768 to reduce internal waste. that is low-risk patch (alloc table change) but needs careful rollover and may increase slab fragmentation at other sizes.
sophia: what about KV eviction/paging interactions? If compaction moves data, does paging get confused? need to ensure page alignment and that our eviction pointers remain valid.
marie: good catch — compactor must write into pre-allocated target slabs and update slot pointers atomically. Also need to ensure we don't increase IO for private deployments with slower storage-backed caches.
dan: maybe two-phase: 1) add a sampling allocator metric to track hot sizes and churn per-size; 2) rollout intermediate bins as a canary; 3) background compactor as opt-in feature for Dedicated/Private initially.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: kv-allocator-bin-384 canary -> staging at 2026-04-12T03:00Z. See run 6133333400.
ashok: action items: marie to add per-bin churn telemetry + sample payloads; dan to draft allocator patch with 384/768 bins; sophia to run end-to-end latency + CPU regressions with 1h longcontext sweep; i'll prototype a low-priority compactor skeleton.
marie: i'll also add a small bench: bench-longcontext --sample-allocs --bin-trace to correlate allocation sites.
sophia: timeline? can we have a canary by next Tues? dan: yes, I can open the PR today and stage tests tomorrow.
marie: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the canary runs. :thumbsup:
